title: Cores, memory and tasks
prompt: This program submits a job with 3 cores, 1g of driver memory (on the G1 collector, so the JVM reports the whole 1g heap), adaptive execution off and 5 shuffle partitions. The job prints its cores and the partitions of `spark.range(0, 30)`, its unified memory pool in MiB, and the task count of each stage of one `groupBy` count. The program prints the exit code, then the job's lines without their `app:` prefix. What does it print? Type each line on its own line.
program:
import os, subprocess

open("/tmp/sizing.py", "w").write("""
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = SparkSession.builder.getOrCreate()
sc = spark.sparkContext
tracker = sc.statusTracker()
pool = sc._jsc.sc().getExecutorMemoryStatus().values().head()._1()
nums = spark.range(0, 30)
print("app:", sc.defaultParallelism, nums.rdd.getNumPartitions())
print("app:", pool // 1024**2)

sc.setJobGroup("buckets", "count per bucket")
nums.selectExpr("id % 4 AS bucket").groupBy("bucket").count().collect()
info = tracker.getJobInfo(tracker.getJobIdsForGroup("buckets")[0])
print("app:", [tracker.getStageInfo(s).numTasks for s in sorted(info.stageIds)])
spark.stop()
""")

env = {**os.environ, "SPARK_LOCAL_IP": "127.0.0.1"}
run = subprocess.run(
    ["spark-submit", "--master", "local[3]", "--driver-memory", "1g", "--driver-java-options", "-XX:+UseG1GC",
     "--conf", "spark.sql.adaptive.enabled=false", "--conf", "spark.sql.shuffle.partitions=5",
     "/tmp/sizing.py"],
    capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
print(run.returncode)
for line in run.stdout.splitlines():
    if line.startswith("app:"):
        print(line[5:])
hints: In local mode the master sets the cores, and `spark.range` without a partition count makes one partition per core.
The pool is (heap - 300 MiB) × 0.6. `--driver-memory 1g` gives a 1024 MiB heap, and G1 reports all of it. Round down.
A `groupBy` count is two stages: one task per input partition, then one task per shuffle partition.
explanation: `local[3]` gives 3 cores, so `defaultParallelism` is 3 and `spark.range(0, 30)` is split into 3 partitions. `--driver-memory 1g` sizes the one JVM: (1024 - 300) × 0.6 = 434.4, so the pool is 434 MiB. The `groupBy` count runs as two stages (lesson 55): 3 tasks over the input partitions, then 5 tasks, one per shuffle partition, because adaptive execution is off and can't merge them. With 3 cores the second stage runs 3 tasks at once, then the last 2: cores limit how many tasks run together, not how many there are.
